description: Cover art for EVERY game, not for the ones whose dumper happened to use the same naming convention as the thumbnail server. The first device run of FEAT-004 resolved real box art for three games out of six, and the user's requirement is verbatim: 'ALL games a user puts in it needs to get the cover art one way or another, I'd prefer a user not have to open the game to get the cover art.' This feature closes that gap in three parts: name forms that REWRITE a naming convention instead of deleting tags, a search of the server's own cover list for the names that cannot be derived at all, and a bounded sweep so a game does not have to be scrolled to, let alone opened, to get its art.

decision_point.question: Three of six games got art. Why those three, and what can reach the other three?
decision_point.what_the_device_run_showed: Working: Crash Bandicoot (USA), Pokemon Emerald (USA, Europe), Mortal Kombat 3 (USA). Not working: Super Mario World (U) [!].smc, Simpsons, The - Krusty's Fun House (U) [!].gg, Kart Fighter.nes. The split is not random and it is not about the system: the three that worked carry No-Intro names, which is what libretro names thumbnails after, and the three that failed carry GoodTools names, '(U)' for USA and '[!]' for a verified dump.
decision_point.the_root_cause: The ladder only ever STRIPPED tags, and stripping is a one way door. '(U)' can become nothing, but it can never become '(USA)'. Measured against the live server rather than reasoned about: 'Super Mario World (U) [!]', 'Super Mario World (U)' and 'Super Mario World' are all 404, and 'Super Mario World (USA)' is a 200 image/png of 301,072 bytes.
decision_point.the_three_failures_are_three_different_p: Super Mario World needs a region code TRANSLATED, which is one extra request. Kart Fighter cannot be reached by any transform at all: the server files it as 'Kart Fighter (199x)(-)(AS)[p].png', a third convention whose date, publisher, country and pirate flag are simply not in the filename on disk, so the only thing that can find it is the server's own list of what it has. Krusty's Fun House has NO Game Gear box art on the server at all: the folder's only Simpsons covers are Bartman Meets Radioactive Man, Bart vs. the Space Mutants and Bart vs. the World. That third one is a real outcome and must stay a plate.
decision_point.recommendation: Add rewriting rungs to the ladder first because they are cheap and fix a whole convention. Add the directory-index search second, once per system, only after every cheap name has 404ed, and match on an EQUALITY of normalised titles so a genuine miss stays a miss. Record the genuine miss in the existing one week negative cache and say so plainly, because inventing a wrong cover by loosening the match until something hits would be worse than a plate.

steps: Add a regionTranslated name form that rewrites GoodTools region codes into the No-Intro spelling, reusing GameMetadata.regionName(forTag:) rather than a second table, so the region a card SHOWS and the region the server is ASKED FOR cannot drift apart. It sits after the dump-tags-dropped form and before the all-tags-dropped one, because a translated name still carries a region and is therefore more specific than a bare title.

Add a regionAppended form that offers (USA), (USA, Europe), (World), (Europe) and (Japan) to a name carrying no region at all, since a No-Intro name almost always has one and the untagged form has none. Gate it on 'the name names no region in either convention', so (Unl) counts as missing a region and (Rev A) is not mistaken for one.
Keep the original three forms and their order, and keep the whole ladder deduped by name and by URL, so a game that already worked asks for nothing more than it did before.

Fetch the system's Named_Boxarts directory index at most once per system, and only when the whole ladder has 404ed. Extract the png filenames by scanning the raw bytes, fold them onto normalised titles, and persist ONLY that map: the HTML is 4,054,023 bytes for the NES and is never stored.

Hold a task per system exactly as the store already holds one per game, so ten cards asking at the same moment cannot become ten multi megabyte downloads. Keep the list for thirty days, with a Settings action to forget it.

Match on an equality of normalised titles: percent-decoded, HTML-unescaped, .png dropped, every parenthesised and bracketed group dropped, diacritics folded, apostrophes deleted, other punctuation spaced, collapsed, lowercased. No substring, no distance threshold.
Break ties deterministically and toward the least decorated file: fewest bracketed groups, then shortest, then alphabetical. A bad dump or a fan translation is not the cover anyone means.

Announce the list download on the artwork line BEFORE it happens, promote the first one of a run to the main status line, disclose it in Settings next to the artwork switch, and report what it cost afterwards.

Sweep the whole library one game at a time so a game that is not on screen still gets its art, which is the half of the user's requirement that the lazy shelves could never satisfy. One at a time is the bound: it leaves two of the three lookup slots for the cards the user is looking at.
Record a genuine miss only when BOTH the ladder and the list search have answered, and never on a failure of either.
acceptance_criteria: A GoodTools named game resolves its real box art: 'Super Mario World (U) [!].smc' produces a candidate named exactly 'Super Mario World (USA)'.
A game named under a convention this app cannot derive still resolves: 'Kart Fighter.nes' finds 'Kart Fighter (199x)(-)(AS)[p].png'.
A game with genuinely no art keeps its plate, is recorded as a miss for a week, and is never given another game's cover.
A system's cover list is downloaded at most once, never twice concurrently, kept for thirty days, and clearable from Settings.
The 4 MB of listing HTML is never stored; only the extracted titles are.
Every game in the library resolves art without being opened and without being scrolled to, and at most three cover lookups are in flight at once.
The list download is disclosed in Settings and reported on the artwork line while it happens.
The existing ladder, its order, the three-at-a-time gate, the one week negative cache and the plate under real art are all unchanged.
verification: The pure functions extracted from the shipped files and RUN on the build host: the name forms and their order, the region translation table, the appended-region gate, the ladder dedupe, the title normalisation, the tie-break, the match, and the picture rect. 73 checks, all passing.

The two big checks run against saved copies of the real thumbnails.libretro.com listings rather than against fixtures: the NES index (4,054,023 bytes, 13,418 png names, 2,935 titles, parsed in 0.29s, kept as 200,861 bytes of JSON, 5.0% of the HTML), the SNES index and the Game Gear index.

The new candidate URLs curled against the live server: 'Super Mario World (USA).png' 200 image/png 301,072 bytes, 'Kart Fighter (199x)(-)(AS)[p].png' 200 image/png 633,956 bytes, all five appended-region Kart Fighter guesses 404, and Krusty's Fun House 404 in all three folders.

swiftc -frontend -parse on every Swift file under native/ios/: exit 0. ArtworkIndex.swift additionally type-checked in full against the real ArtworkNames, SystemArtwork and GameMetadata, with only two Linux platform artefacts patched in the copy (the FoundationNetworking import and waitsForConnectivity, which is settable on Darwin and is set the same way by the shipped ArtworkFetcher.session).
cargo test: 74 passing, proving no Rust changed.

On device, still to be confirmed by the user: all six games showing art or a plate with a reason, the first list download appearing on the status line, and the picture centred in the space above the controls.
findings: Implemented in native/ios/GameArtwork.swift (two new rungs), native/ios/ArtworkIndex.swift (new: the list parse, the match, the thirty day store) and native/ios/ArtworkStore.swift (the discipline around both, plus the sweep). THE REGION TABLE IS NOT A SECOND TABLE: ArtworkNames.translateRegionCodes calls GameMetadata.regionName(forTag:), which already turns '(U)' into 'USA' for the metadata line under every card, so the region a card shows and the region the server is asked for are one value. The new rungs cost nothing for a game that already worked, because the ladder dedupes by name and a No-Intro name translates to itself: 'Tetris (World).nes' still costs two forms and six candidates. THE HONESTY SAFEGUARD IS AN EQUALITY, not a threshold: 'simpsons the krustys fun house' is not equal to 'simpsons the bart vs the world', so Krusty's Fun House matches nothing in a Game Gear folder that really does have three other Simpsons covers, and it is recorded as a genuine miss with a status line that says the list was searched. THE TIE-BREAK WAS TESTED AGAINST THE SEVEN REAL KART FIGHTER FILES, not against invented ones, and picks '(199x)(-)(AS)[p]' over the [b], [b2], [b3] bad dumps and the three [tr ...] translations, and picks the same one whichever order the listing arrives in. WHAT IS KEPT IS THE MAP AND NOT THE PAGE: 4,054,023 bytes of NES HTML becomes 200,861 bytes of JSON, 5.0%, measured rather than estimated. The list download runs OUTSIDE ArtworkGate on its own session with a 180 second resource timeout, because holding one of three lookup slots for a multi megabyte download would starve the visible cards, while the matched cover's fetch takes a slot like every other lookup. One task per system, inserted with no await between the dictionary check and the insertion, so ten cards cannot become ten downloads. A miss is now recorded only when both the ladder and the list search have honestly answered no; a list that could not be downloaded reports itself and records nothing, because a week of plates must not be a conclusion drawn from a failure. ArtworkDisk.clear() and usage() now skip directories, which is load-bearing rather than tidy: the lists live in Artwork/CoverLists and removeItem on a directory is recursive, so without it 'clear artwork cache' would silently throw away the megabytes of list downloads too. The sweep is triggered from refreshLibrary, which runs at launch and after every import, delete and return from a game; it waits two seconds to let the import summary and the visible cards go first, is cancelled and restarted by the next rescan, checks memory then the negative cache then the system then a non-decoding disk check before it touches the network, and bumps the artwork generation in batches of four so covers it finds appear on cards that had already resolved to a plate.
